data.summary: The three‑week plan front‑loads the weak Unit 2 topics, then moves through core mechanics before a mixed review in the final week. Each week stays within the 7‑hour limit, combines live class participation, focused practice, and timed free‑response drills.

weeks.focus: Build foundational understanding of forces and Newton's laws (Unit 2).
tasks: Watch the live Class 10100 recording and take detailed notes on free‑body diagrams and Newton's Second Law.
Do 12 free‑response questions on free‑body diagrams (FRQs from past AP exams), then compare answers with the scoring guide (≈2 h).
Complete 8 problems applying F=ma to inclined planes and tension systems (≈1.5 h).
Create a one‑page cheat sheet summarizing the steps for solving force problems (≈0.5 h).
Review class notes and cheat sheet, then take a 20‑minute timed quiz on 5 mixed force problems (≈1 h).

weeks.focus: Integrate kinematics and energy concepts to broaden mechanics foundation.
tasks: Read textbook sections on Scalars/Vectors and Displacement/Velocity/Acceleration; annotate examples (≈1 h).
Complete 10 graph‑interpretation problems for motion (≈1 h).
Do 8 free‑response questions on kinematic equations, then self‑grade with the AP scoring rubric (≈1.5 h).
Study Translational Kinetic Energy and Work; watch a short Khan Academy video on work‑energy theorem (≈0.5 h).
Solve 10 work‑energy problems involving ramps and pulleys, checking answers with solution manual (≈1.5 h).
Take a 15‑minute timed mixed set of 5 kinematics + 5 work‑energy FRQs (≈1 h).

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed practice covering all units studied.
tasks: Review notes and cheat sheets from Units 2, 1, and 3 (≈1 h).
Do a set of 6 mixed FRQs: 2 on systems/center of mass, 2 on Newton's laws, 1 on linear momentum, 1 on rotational kinematics (≈2 h).
Mark each response against the AP scoring guide and note any recurring errors (≈1 h).
Complete 5 quick‑fire multiple‑choice drills covering fluids, oscillations, and torque (≈0.5 h).
Run a full 90‑minute timed practice exam (selected past FRQs) to simulate test conditions (≈2 h).
Spend the final 0.5 h reviewing the practice exam results and updating the cheat sheet with any missed concepts.

data.final_week_advice: In the last week, focus on consolidating knowledge, identifying lingering weak spots, and practicing under timed conditions. Use the cheat sheet for quick reference, and simulate exam stamina with a full‑length practice test.
